habitats: Coastal spray belt above mean high tide
Sea-arch and islet margins above regular inundation
summary: A sprawling evergreen succulent shrub, 0.3–1.2 m tall, with salt-beaded leaves and rooted woody runners. It occupies drained spray-zone ground above mean high tide, supplying salt and low shaded cover. Storm washover can kill patches; it is not a submerged coastal plant (F19, F20, F23).

links: Marine spray loads foliage and rooting ground with salt.
Ion compartmentation and gland secretion control internal salt concentrations.
Fleshy leaves store water while secreted droplets evaporate into collectible crystals.
chains.play: Scrape dry leaf margins for salt and inspect browsed tips for coloso visits.
chains.weakness: Rain removes collectible crystals; prolonged flooding overwhelms roots, and storm washover can kill whole patches.
observe: Clear droplets gather beside old white crystals.
Rain washes the rims away while leaves remain firm.

plausibility.summary: Rooting sites remain above mean high tide in the spray belt. Salt tolerance does not confer regular submergence tolerance; salt is a mineral reward rather than an alkaloid defence.

analogues.organism: Salt-excreting Limonium species and succulent coastal halophytes
analogues.mechanism: Ion regulation, compartmentation, secretion and succulence provide complementary mechanisms for tolerating saline terrestrial habitats.

chains.trait: Low woody runners with multiple rooting points
links: Dense-air winds impose strong loads on coastal shoots.
A low crown reduces projected area and bending leverage.
Buried nodes distribute anchorage and support shaded spaces beneath overlapping branches.
chains.play: Use mature crowns for low visual cover and shade.
chains.weakness: Scour can undermine rooting pockets; low crowns conceal only suitably small bodies.
observe: Seaward branches lie lower than sheltered shoots.
A buried runner roots at several nodes.

plausibility.summary: Low geometry and distributed anchorage reduce wind damage without preventing storm losses. Shade does not erase scent trails.

analogues.mechanism: Reduced projected area, flexible reconfiguration and distributed rooting limit mechanical loading.

poison.signal: Glaucous green leaves with white salt beads; no persistent red-veined alkaloid warning.

gameplay.cover: Low visual cover and shade beneath sprawling crowns.
gameplay.nest_material: Dry fine twigs above the storm-wrack line.
gameplay.mineral_lick: Salt crystals on leaves and older stems.
gameplay.notes: Excess consumption imposes a salt load. Rain reduces harvest without inherently causing wilt. Repeated tidal flooding excludes establishment.

relations.note: Browses succulent tips and obtains surface salt.
Provides coastal shade; each albino retains its base species' diet.
Conceals small individuals above tidal feeding grounds.
Forms the terrestrial spray belt above regularly flooded algae.

generator.trunk: Several short woody bases connected by surface runners.

branching.buttress: None; buried nodes form adventitious roots.

overlay_rules: White crystals accumulate at gland-bearing margins after drying.
Rain removes the crystals without changing living leaf colour.

placement.slope: Stable sediment pockets on 0–35 degree coastal slopes; exclude active scour.
placement.wetness: Drained spray-zone ground strictly above local mean high tide; exclude regularly flooded sites.
placement.soil: Rock fissures, coarse sand and sediment pockets without active geothermal contamination.
placement.fog: Tolerates marine fog, which alone does not create salt crystals.
placement.density: Irregular sprawling patches within the above-high-tide habitat mask.

generator.seasonal: Evergreen; grows after sustained rain. Winter storms remove tips and can kill washed-over patches.
generator.wind_response: Outer shoots flex near the ground; crowns become asymmetric toward shelter.

journal.en: The bush leaves salt on its lips. Beneath it, even the pale ones can rest.
journal.es: El arbusto deja sal en sus labios. Debajo, hasta los pálidos pueden descansar.

changelog.what: flora pass: 7 voices drafted and peer-reviewed, Composer botanical referee, sol chaired and applied the fixes

observe: White-rimmed shrubs grow above the regularly wetted shore.
Washed outer leaves lack crystals retained inside the crown.
Rooted runners connect apparently separate crowns.
secrets: Inner leaves can retain crystals after a light shower.
Repeated browsing reveals a coastal mineral route used by coloso.
